rows: Makkan according to the stronger view; some scholars classify it as Madinan.
One of the two al-Muʿawwidhatayn (the two chapters of seeking protection).
Seeking Allah's protection from hidden, harmful suggestions arising among jinn and people.
Imperative and present verbs; genitive constructions; apposition/description; relative pronoun; quadriliteral verb; broken plural.

blocks.text: No specific occasion of revelation is established with sufficient certainty to be presented as an undisputed cause for Sūrat al-Nās. Some reports link the two protective surahs to the incident of sorcery against the Prophet ﷺ, but the historical incident and a claim about the surahs' precise occasion of revelation are distinct matters. Ibn ʿĀshūr questions that connection. We therefore do not teach it as settled fact.
Read all six verses accurately and explain their connected meaning.
Understand every Qur'anic word in this surah using simple English and Arabic glosses.
Recognize the imperative قُلْ, the present verbs أَعُوذُ and يُوَسْوِسُ, and the four-letter verb وَسْوَسَ.
Identify genitive nouns, iḍāfah, adjectives and a relative clause.
Notice the repeated ٱلنَّاسِ and the three descriptions رَبِّ، مَلِكِ، إِلَـٰهِ.

Study note: This is the opening lesson in our sequence. All Qur'anic example phrases in the lesson come from Sūrat al-Nās. Additional verb forms are labelled as language forms, not quoted Qur'anic verses.
قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلنَّاسِ  ﴿1﴾
Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of humankind.

rows: In / with the Lord and Sustainer

blocks.text: Allah teaches the Prophet, and through him every believer, to turn to Him for protection. The act of seeking refuge is expressed directly in the first person: ‘I seek refuge.’
قُلْ is an imperative (فِعْلُ أَمْرٍ). Its understood subject is ‘you’ (أَنْتَ).
أَعُوذُ is a present-tense verb (فِعْلٌ مُضَارِعٌ), first-person singular. Its subject is understood as أَنَا.
The preposition بِـ makes رَبِّ genitive (مَجْرُورًا). رَبِّ is also the first member (مُضَاف) of the phrase رَبِّ ٱلنَّاسِ, and ٱلنَّاسِ is مُضَافٌ إِلَيْهِ.
قُلْ comes from قَالَ / يَقُولُ (root ق و ل), a Form I hollow verb (فِعْلٌ أَجْوَفُ).
أَعُوذُ comes from عَاذَ / يَعُوذُ (root ع و ذ), also a Form I hollow verb.
رَبّ is a noun associated with the root ر ب ب; ٱلنَّاسِ is a plural/collective designation for people.

rows: to seek refuge; 1st-person form in the verse

blocks.text: The listed forms are morphological study forms. Only the exact word shown in the verse strip is Qur'anic text from this passage.
The direct command قُلْ gives the learner words to use. Beginning with Allah's lordship establishes the source of the sought protection.
One Arabic word can contain a prefixed particle and a noun: بِرَبِّ combines بِـ with رَبِّ. In an iḍāfah, the second noun is genitive.
مَلِكِ ٱلنَّاسِ  ﴿2﴾
The Sovereign of humankind.
The One whose protection is sought is not only the Lord who nurtures people; He also possesses complete authority over them.
مَلِكِ is genitive because it further describes or clarifies رَبِّ in verse 1. It may be analysed as a substitute (بَدَل), an explanatory apposition (عَطْفُ بَيَان), or an adjective (نَعْت).
مَلِكِ ٱلنَّاسِ is another possessive/association construction (إِضَافَة): مَلِكِ is مُضَاف and ٱلنَّاسِ is مُضَافٌ إِلَيْهِ.
مَلِك is a noun built from root م ل ك. It is not a finite verb in this verse.
There is no explicit finite verb in this verse. / لَا يُوجَدُ فِعْلٌ صَرِيحٌ فِي هَذِهِ الْآيَةِ.
The description moves from the Lord who cares for people to the Sovereign who rules them. Repeating ٱلنَّاسِ keeps the group receiving that care and authority explicit.
The grammar can continue across verse boundaries: مَلِكِ is linked to رَبِّ in the previous verse, not an independent nominative word.
إِلَـٰهِ ٱلنَّاسِ  ﴿3﴾
The God of humankind, worthy of their worship.
Allah is the true God of all people, so seeking His protection is an act of worship and reliance upon Him.
إِلَـٰهِ is genitive as a further explanation of رَبِّ (and of the sequence مَلِكِ); the grammarians also allow بدل, عطف بيان and نعت analyses.
إِلَـٰهِ ٱلنَّاسِ is an iḍāfah construction, and ٱلنَّاسِ is genitive as مُضَافٌ إِلَيْهِ.
إِلَٰه is a noun (اسْم), not a verb. The verse uses it in a genitive form: إِلَٰهِ.
There is no explicit finite verb in this verse. / لَا يُوجَدُ فِعْلٌ صَرِيحٌ فِي هَذِهِ الْآيَةِ.
The three successive descriptions — رَبِّ، مَلِكِ، إِلَـٰهِ — present care, authority and the right to be worshipped. This is a meaningful progression, not a list of unrelated titles.
The same noun ٱلنَّاسِ appears in verses 1, 2 and 3, each time after a different preceding noun.
مِن شَرِّ ٱلْوَسْوَاسِ ٱلْخَنَّاسِ  ﴿4﴾
From the evil of the whisperer who withdraws.

rows: حَرْفُ جَرٍّ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الِاسْتِعَاذَةِ مِنَ الشَّرِّ
The whisperer; one who repeatedly whispers
The one who retreats or hides

blocks.text: The believer asks to be protected from harmful, quiet suggestions that lead toward wrong actions. The whisperer is called ‘one who withdraws’ because he retreats when Allah is remembered.
مِن is a preposition. It makes شَرِّ genitive; شَرِّ is also مُضَاف.
ٱلْوَسْوَاسِ is مُضَافٌ إِلَيْهِ and is genitive. ٱلْخَنَّاسِ is an adjective (نَعْت) describing it, so it is genitive too.
The phrase مِن شَرِّ is grammatically connected to أَعُوذُ in verse 1, although three verses intervene.
ٱلْوَسْوَاس is derived from the four-letter verb وَسْوَسَ (root و س و س). Here the noun denotes the whisperer.
ٱلْخَنَّاس is on the intensive pattern فَعَّال from root خ ن س, indicating frequent or characteristic withdrawal.
There is no explicit finite verb in this verse. / لَا يُوجَدُ فِعْلٌ صَرِيحٌ فِي هَذِهِ الْآيَةِ.
The paired expressions ٱلْوَسْوَاسِ and ٱلْخَنَّاسِ describe an adversary who both whispers and draws back, giving a vivid picture of hidden influence.
The grammatical relation introduced by a verb may extend beyond a single verse; this is why reading the entire passage helps more than isolated word translation.
ٱلَّذِى يُوَسْوِسُ فِى صُدُورِ ٱلنَّاسِ  ﴿5﴾
Who whispers into the inner hearts of humankind.
The verse tells us how the whisperer acts: he places hidden suggestions in people's inner lives and thoughts, rather than necessarily speaking aloud.
ٱلَّذِى is a relative pronoun (اسْمٌ مَوْصُول) in a genitive syntactic position, describing ٱلْوَسْوَاسِ.
يُوَسْوِسُ is a present-tense verb with a hidden third-person masculine subject, هُوَ; the verbal clause is the relative clause (صِلَةُ الْمَوْصُول).
فِى is a preposition; صُدُورِ is genitive and مُضَاف; ٱلنَّاسِ is its genitive مُضَافٌ إِلَيْهِ.
وَسْوَسَ / يُوَسْوِسُ is a four-radical (رُبَاعِيّ) verb, patterned فَعْلَلَ / يُفَعْلِلُ, not a triliteral Form II verb.
صُدُور is the broken plural (جَمْعُ تَكْسِير) of صَدْر on the pattern فُعُول.

rows: to whisper; 3rd-person present in the verse

blocks.text: The listed forms are morphological study forms. Only the exact word shown in the verse strip is Qur'anic text from this passage.
The relative clause gives a precise description of the hidden action. The phrase فِى صُدُورِ directs attention to the inward place where suggestions are received.
Arabic has four-letter verb roots as well as three-letter roots. Recognising the repeated consonants in وَسْوَسَ helps identify the word family.
مِنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ  ﴿6﴾
From among jinn and humankind.
The closing words make clear that harmful suggestions can come from jinn and from human beings. The believer seeks Allah's protection from both.
مِنَ is a preposition and ٱلْجِنَّةِ is its genitive noun. The و in وَٱلنَّاسِ is a coordinating conjunction; ٱلنَّاسِ is also genitive.
In detailed iʿrāb, مِنَ can be understood as explanatory (بَيَانِيَّة), or as indicating origin or part of a group. These alternatives belong in the companion Iʿrāb Book.
ٱلْجِنَّةِ denotes the jinn in this context. Its initial vowel is kasrah: الْجِنَّة, not a word for a garden or paradise.
There is no explicit finite verb in this verse. / لَا يُوجَدُ فِعْلٌ صَرِيحٌ فِي هَذِهِ الْآيَةِ.
Ending with both ٱلْجِنَّةِ and ٱلنَّاسِ broadens the warning to visible and unseen sources of temptation and completes the surah's protective prayer.
Paying attention to vowels changes meaning. In this verse the word ٱلْجِنَّةِ refers to jinn; it should not be read with a different initial vowel.

This is a complete review of the six verses. Read the whole surah aloud first. Then connect its meaning, words, grammar, verb forms and rhetorical features before answering the 20 multiple-choice questions below.

Sūrat al-Nās is chapter 114 of the Qur'an, with six verses in Juzʾ 30. It is one of the two al-Muʿawwidhatayn. The stronger classification is Makkan, though there is scholarly disagreement. No particular event should be taught as an undisputed occasion of its revelation. Its central message is to seek the protection of Allah — the Lord, Sovereign and God of humankind — from harmful suggestions associated with the whisperer, whether their source is among jinn or people.

title.en: The meaning of all six verses

rows: A direct command to seek protection in Allah's lordship.
Allah's complete sovereignty and authority over people.
Allah alone is the God worthy of worship.
The harmful whisperer, who retreats or withdraws.
The hidden action of whispering in people's inward lives.
The sources mentioned include jinn and human beings.

blocks.text: Important connection: verses 2 and 3 continue the description of رَبِّ in verse 1; مِن شَرِّ in verse 4 is connected to أَعُوذُ; and verse 5 describes the whisperer in verse 4. The verse endings do not break these grammatical links.

The second noun is مُضَافٌ إِلَيْهِ

The opening قُلْ teaches the very words of seeking refuge.
The order is رَبِّ first, then مَلِكِ, then إِلَـٰهِ: from lordship and care to authority and worship.
ٱلنَّاسِ appears five times, directly reinforcing each connection to humankind.
The paired terms ٱلْوَسْوَاسِ and ٱلْخَنَّاسِ create the picture of repeated whispering and withdrawal.
The relative clause ٱلَّذِى يُوَسْوِسُ identifies the whisperer through his action.
The final mention of jinn and people includes unseen and human sources of harmful suggestions.
Read vowels carefully: ٱلْجِنَّةِ here denotes jinn, not a garden; بِرَبِّ contains a prefixed preposition and a noun.

blocks.text: The nominal expressions in this surah occur within genitive structures: after prepositions, in iḍāfah, or as words grammatically linked to those nouns. Its imperative and present verbs are distinct from these nominal forms.
قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلنَّاسِ  ﴿1﴾
Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of humankind.

rows: فِعْلُ أَمْرٍ مَبْنِيٌّ عَلَى السُّكُونِ؛ فَاعِلُهُ ضَمِيرٌ مُسْتَتِرٌ وُجُوبًا تَقْدِيرُهُ أَنْتَ.

Present; hidden first-person subject. The clause is what is said.
حَرْفُ جَرٍّ مَبْنِيٌّ لَا مَحَلَّ لَهُ مِنَ الْإِعْرَابِ.
اسْمٌ مَجْرُورٌ بِالْبَاءِ، وَعَلَامَةُ جَرِّهِ الْكَسْرَةُ؛ وَهُوَ مُضَافٌ. وَالْجَارُّ وَالْمَجْرُورُ مُتَعَلِّقَانِ بِأَعُوذُ.
Genitive after بِـ; first term of iḍāfah.

blocks.text: Sentence relation: the clause أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلنَّاسِ is the content of the command قُلْ; the prepositional phrase بِرَبِّ is linked to أَعُوذُ.
مَلِكِ ٱلنَّاسِ  ﴿2﴾
The Sovereign of humankind.

rows: بَدَلٌ مَجْرُورٌ مِنْ رَبِّ، وَعَلَامَةُ جَرِّهِ الْكَسْرَةُ، وَهُوَ مُضَافٌ. وَيَجُوزُ إِعْرَابُهُ نَعْتًا أَوْ عَطْفَ بَيَانٍ.
Genitive apposition to رَبِّ; alternative modifier analyses.

blocks.text: Teaching note: the case continues from verse 1. The three expressions رَبِّ / مَلِكِ / إِلَـٰهِ are not three unrelated nominative statements.
إِلَـٰهِ ٱلنَّاسِ  ﴿3﴾
The God of humankind, worthy of their worship.

rows: بَدَلٌ مَجْرُورٌ مِنْ رَبِّ أَوْ مِمَّا قَبْلَهُ، وَهُوَ مُضَافٌ؛ وَيَجُوزُ فِيهِ عَطْفُ الْبَيَانِ وَالنَّعْتُ.
Genitive apposition continuing the same construction.

blocks.text: Teaching note: the case continues from verse 1. The three expressions رَبِّ / مَلِكِ / إِلَـٰهِ are not three unrelated nominative statements.
مِن شَرِّ ٱلْوَسْوَاسِ ٱلْخَنَّاسِ  ﴿4﴾
From the evil of the whisperer who withdraws.

rows: حَرْفُ جَرٍّ مَبْنِيٌّ لَا مَحَلَّ لَهُ مِنَ الْإِعْرَابِ.
اسْمٌ مَجْرُورٌ بِمِنْ، وَعَلَامَةُ جَرِّهِ الْكَسْرَةُ، وَهُوَ مُضَافٌ.
Genitive after مِن; first member of iḍāfah.
نَعْتٌ مَجْرُورٌ لِلْوَسْوَاسِ، وَعَلَامَةُ جَرِّهِ الْكَسْرَةُ.

blocks.text: Sentence relation: مِن شَرِّ ... is another phrase governed by أَعُوذُ from verse 1; the noun ٱلْخَنَّاسِ follows the case of the noun it describes.
ٱلَّذِى يُوَسْوِسُ فِى صُدُورِ ٱلنَّاسِ  ﴿5﴾
Who whispers into the inner hearts of humankind.

rows: اسْمٌ مَوْصُولٌ مَبْنِيٌّ عَلَى السُّكُونِ فِي مَحَلِّ جَرٍّ نَعْتٌ لِلْوَسْوَاسِ. وَرُوِيَتْ أَوْجُهٌ إِعْرَابِيَّةٌ أُخْرَى.
Relative pronoun in the genitive position of a modifier.
فِعْلٌ مُضَارِعٌ مَرْفُوعٌ بِالضَّمَّةِ؛ فَاعِلُهُ ضَمِيرٌ مُسْتَتِرٌ تَقْدِيرُهُ هُوَ. وَجُمْلَتُهُ صِلَةُ الْمَوْصُولِ لَا مَحَلَّ لَهَا.
Present verb; its clause completes ٱلَّذِى.
حَرْفُ جَرٍّ مَبْنِيٌّ لَا مَحَلَّ لَهُ.
اسْمٌ مَجْرُورٌ بِفِي، وَعَلَامَةُ جَرِّهِ الْكَسْرَةُ، وَهُوَ مُضَافٌ.
Genitive after فِى; broken plural of صَدْر.

blocks.text: Other recognised analyses permit a nominative or accusative resumption of ٱلَّذِى in an evaluative construction. The genitive modifier analysis is the most straightforward for this lesson.
مِنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ  ﴿6﴾
From among jinn and humankind.

rows: حَرْفُ جَرٍّ؛ وَفُتِحَتْ نُونُهُ لِالْتِقَاءِ السَّاكِنَيْنِ. وَمِنْ أَوْجُهِهِ أَنْ تَكُونَ بَيَانِيَّةً أَوِ ابْتِدَائِيَّةً أَوْ تَبْعِيضِيَّةً.
اسْمٌ مَجْرُورٌ بِمِنْ، وَعَلَامَةُ جَرِّهِ الْكَسْرَةُ الظَّاهِرَةُ.
حَرْفُ عَطْفٍ مَبْنِيٌّ لَا مَحَلَّ لَهُ.
اسْمٌ مَعْطُوفٌ عَلَى ٱلْجِنَّةِ مَجْرُورٌ بِالْكَسْرَةِ.

blocks.text: Alternative connections of مِنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ include an explanatory phrase describing the whisperer, or a phrase indicating the source of whispering. Some grammarians attach it to an understood circumstantial expression (حَال). These are interpretive grammatical alternatives, not different Qur'anic wordings.
قُلْ → its spoken content is أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلنَّاسِ ...
أَعُوذُ → governs بِرَبِّ ٱلنَّاسِ and مِن شَرِّ ٱلْوَسْوَاسِ ...
رَبِّ → is clarified by مَلِكِ and إِلَـٰهِ, both genitive in the connected construction.
ٱلْوَسْوَاسِ → is described by ٱلْخَنَّاسِ and by the relative clause ٱلَّذِى يُوَسْوِسُ ...
يُوَسْوِسُ → is connected with فِى صُدُورِ ٱلنَّاسِ; the final مِنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ further clarifies source/identity.

rows: Imperative of hollow Form I verb قَالَ
Broken plural on فُعُول; singular صَدْر
